clue.text: What a lifer does as part of keep fit?

definitions.meaning: a prisoner serving life does a lengthy spell inside, slang for a long prison sentence
an exercise routine includes reaching and extending the body at length

explanation.surface: A prisoner serving life does some exercises as part of a fitness routine in the jail.
explanation.definitionFit: Stretch is slang for a prison term, and a long one is a life sentence; in a workout it is literally an extended pull of the muscles.

clue.text: A bogus journalist getting red-faced

parts.note: something bogus is a sham, a fake
ED is short for editor, the crossword's usual journalist

explanation.surface: A fake reporter is caught out and blushes with embarrassment.
explanation.definitionFit: Being red-faced is blushing from embarrassment or guilt, the feeling of shame.

clue.text: Heading for 50th? Leave it out, that's ancient!

indicators.note: the heading of the word for a 50th anniversary is its first letter, the one to drop
an order to omit something, here the initial letter just named

parts.note: a golden anniversary or jubilee marks fifty years

explanation.surface: Someone nearing fifty is told to stop going on about it, since that already sounds old.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heading for 50th' reads as approaching fifty, but it names the head letter G of GOLDEN; 'Leave it out' drops it.
explanation.definitionFit: Olden is an old-fashioned adjective for long past, as in olden days, so it means ancient.

clue.text: Garbed for a change in Eastern fabric

indicators.note: doing something for a change means doing it differently, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
E is the abbreviation for East or Eastern

explanation.surface: Someone dresses differently for once, in an oriental fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Garbed' looks like part of the dressing-up picture, but 'for a change' marks it as letters to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Gaberdine is a tightly woven twill cloth used for raincoats, so it is a type of fabric.

clue.text: Loss of old husband from depression: remains found in garden receptacle

indicators.note: losing something means it is taken away, so these letters are removed from the word that follows 'from'

parts.note: a trough is a low point or a hollow, a depression
H is the abbreviation for husband in genealogy

explanation.surface: A widow, depressed after losing her elderly husband, buries his remains in a garden container.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Loss of' takes O and H out of TROUGH, leaving TRUG; 'remains found in' just links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A trug is a shallow wooden basket gardeners use for carrying flowers and produce, a British garden item.

clue.text: Page bound not to be read

definitions.text: Page bound not to be read

parts.words: Page bound not to be read
parts.note: a blank leaf glued inside the cover at each end of a book is bound in with the rest but carries no text

explanation.surface: A page in a book that nobody is meant to read.
explanation.definitionFit: The blank sheet pasted to the inside of a hardback's cover is bound into the volume but carries nothing to read.

clue.text: Butterfly — also a sign one's turned up in 23 Across

definitions.meaning: a European butterfly with ragged orange wings and a white mark under the hind wing

definitions.text: a sign one's turned up in 23 Across
definitions.meaning: the clue to 23 Across sits in quotation marks, and the opening mark is the punctuation sign flipped and raised

explanation.surface: A butterfly appears, and also a mark showing one has arrived somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: The 23 Across clue opens with an inverted mark: the same sign raised and rotated. The cross-reference is to the clue's printed punctuation, not its answer.
explanation.definitionFit: It is both the name of a butterfly with a tiny pale mark under its wing and the punctuation mark that separates clauses.

clue.text: Parsons maybe going commando for crying out loud!

indicators.note: an exclamation that literally means 'when shouted out', so the words are heard rather than read

parts.note: going commando is slang for wearing no underwear, being without knickers

explanation.surface: An exasperated cry at a parson who goes without underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Parsons' looks like clergymen, but it is the surname of Nicholas Parsons, the long-time host of the BBC radio panel game Just a Minute.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicholas Parsons was a British broadcaster, so his first name is an example with 'maybe' marking it.

clue.text: Note romantic name for diamonds

indicators.note: one thing given for another is a swap, so one letter here replaces the other

parts.note: tender means loving or sentimental
D is the abbreviation for diamonds, the card suit

explanation.surface: A lover writes a note giving a romantic pet name for diamonds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'name for diamonds' looks like a nickname, but 'for' is a swap: N replaces D in TENDER.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenner is British slang for a ten-pound banknote.

clue.text: Kid perhaps destined to be conventional

parts.note: kid is the skin of a young goat used as leather, an example of an animal hide
bound means certain or destined, as in bound to happen

explanation.surface: A child seems fated to grow up conformist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kid' looks like a child; here it is goatskin leather.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone hidebound is narrow and rigidly attached to tradition, so they are conventional in outlook.

clue.text: Me self-consciously about to get silk?

parts.note: moi is the French word for me, used in English in a coy or affected way
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Someone coyly asks whether they might be given silk.
explanation.definitionFit: Moire is watered silk with a rippled sheen; the question mark flags that it is one kind of silk.

clue.text: Endlessly vamp chant

indicators.note: without its end, so the final letter of the synonym is cut off

parts.note: a vamp is a seductive woman who traps men, a mantrap

explanation.surface: A seductress keeps chanting without end.
explanation.definitionFit: A mantra is a word or sound repeated in meditation, a form of chant.

clue.text: Maria not one to put on scanty thong in the long run

indicators.note: saying 'not one' takes the single letter for one out of the name

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: scanty means skimpy or cut short, so the word loses its last letter

explanation.surface: Maria refuses to wear skimpy underwear over a long period.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the long run' looks like 'eventually', but 'the long run' defines a race of 26.2 miles.
explanation.definitionFit: This road race over about 26 miles is the long run of athletics.

clue.text: Confer with writer about proofing

parts.note: to dub is to confer a title or knighthood on someone

indicators.note: about means turned around, so the word for writer is read backwards

parts.note: a nib is the writing point of a pen

explanation.surface: Consult an author about the proofreading of a manuscript.
explanation.walkthrough: 'proofing' looks like checking proofs; it means waterproofing.
explanation.definitionFit: Dubbin is a grease rubbed into leather boots to keep the water out, so it is a waterproofing.

clue.text: Where a sparrow might take a duck

definitions.text: Where a sparrow might take a duck

parts.words: Where a sparrow might take a duck
parts.note: taking a duck here means taking a dip, as small garden visitors splash in a shallow basin

explanation.surface: A puzzling image of a small songbird making off with a larger waterbird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take a duck' suggests seizing a waterbird; it means ducking under water, a quick dip.
explanation.definitionFit: A shallow garden basin of water where small wild visitors bathe and drink.

clue.text: Shop hand, one working on attachment thanks to farmer's wife?

definitions.meaning: someone who sells goods to the public, a shopkeeper or trader

definitions.text: one working on attachment thanks to farmer's wife?
definitions.meaning: in the nursery rhyme Three Blind Mice the farmer's wife cuts off their tails, so someone would need to fix them back on

explanation.surface: A shop assistant on placement, there thanks to a farmer's wife.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as RE-TAILER, it is one who puts tails back on, after the farmer's wife in Three Blind Mice cut them off with a carving knife.
explanation.definitionFit: A seller of goods to the public is a trader or shopkeeper; cryptically, a person who puts severed rear appendages back.

clue.text: Western Avenue in the news or half of Great North Road with better reason

indicators.note: news is spoken on radio and television, so the road number is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: Western Avenue is a stretch of the A40 trunk road in west London, said as 'A forty'
taken as written
the Great North Road is the A1 from London to Edinburgh; half of A1 is the 1, the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A list of British road routes, as if from a traffic bulletin.
explanation.definitionFit: This Latin phrase is used to argue that something holds all the more strongly, with stronger grounds.

clue.text: Mob's coup plea concocted

indicators.note: something concocted is made up or cooked up, so the letters are put together anew

explanation.surface: A gang's plea for a coup is invented.
explanation.definitionFit: The populace is the general public, the masses, which is what mob can mean.

clue.text: Raucous antelopes voiced in trailer?

indicators.note: voiced means spoken, so the words are heard rather than spelt

parts.note: raucous means hoarse, and boks are South African antelopes, as in springbok

explanation.surface: Noisy antelopes being heard in a film trailer.
explanation.definitionFit: A horsebox is a vehicle or towed van for transporting horses; the question mark flags that it is one kind of towed carriage.

clue.text: Superficially tinker inside bonnet of American souped-up car

indicators.note: one thing inside another sits within it, so these letters go into the next word

parts.note: the bonnet of a car is called a hood in American English

indicators.note: on the surface only, so just the outer letters of the word

explanation.surface: A mechanic fiddles a little under the hood of an American muscle car.
explanation.definitionFit: A hot rod is a car modified for extra speed and power, the kind called souped-up.

clue.text: Habitual pretender: old-maidish and head of school in addition

parts.note: po is short for po-faced, prim and humourless

indicators.note: the head of a word is its leading letter, so just the start of school is taken

parts.note: a sum is an addition of numbers

explanation.surface: A habitual fraud is prim and also heads a school.
explanation.walkthrough: Playing dead is this animal's defence, hence 'playing possum' for feigning.
explanation.definitionFit: The opossum feigns death when threatened, so it is a creature that pretends by habit.

clue.text: Is across the Channel in nothing less than moody reserve

indicators.note: one item placed in another sits inside it
less means minus, so a letter is taken away from the word

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing
est is French for 'is', France being across the English Channel

explanation.surface: A sulky Frenchman shows nothing but moody reticence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'less than' takes one O out of MOODY, leaving MODY; 'in' puts EST into it.
explanation.definitionFit: Modesty is reticence about oneself, the restraint that reserve also names.

clue.text: Lumpy, bumpy bus route

indicators.note: a bumpy ride jolts things about, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A rough, uneven ride along a bus route.
explanation.definitionFit: Tuberous means having swellings like tubers, knobbly, so it is lumpy.

clue.text: With long legs raced extremely gracefully

parts.note: ran is the past tense of run, raced

indicators.note: at its extremes, so only the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: A long-legged animal ran with great grace.
explanation.definitionFit: Rangy describes someone tall and slim with long limbs.

clue.text: 'Be all ears' at 10 Down

parts.note: ten written as a word

explanation.surface: A cross-reference instruction telling the solver to listen up at another clue.
explanation.walkthrough: '10 Down' looks like a cross-reference to another clue, but it is TEN and D.
explanation.definitionFit: To be all ears is to listen carefully, to pay attention to someone.

clue.text: Fragrant resin laurel emits internally

indicators.note: on the inside, so the letters lie within these words

explanation.surface: A laurel bush gives off a sweet-smelling sap.
explanation.definitionFit: Elemi is an aromatic gum resin from tropical trees, used in varnishes and perfumes.

clue.text: Feller occasionally a parasite

indicators.note: now and then, so only every other letter is used

explanation.surface: A man is sometimes a hanger-on.
explanation.definitionFit: This small jumping insect feeds on the blood of its hosts, a typical parasite.

clue.text: 0-12″ space in numerous cases

parts.note: zero looks like the letter O
twelve inches make a foot, abbreviated FT
an en is a printer's space half an em wide

explanation.surface: A measurement range up to a foot, with space in many cases.
explanation.definitionFit: Often means frequently, happening on many occasions.

clue.text: Small core affected everyone present

indicators.note: affected means altered or acted upon, so the letters are changed in order

explanation.surface: A small central group was influenced by every person there.
explanation.definitionFit: All-comers means anyone who turns up, every person taking part.

clue.text: Minute edited from chirpy daytime broadcast is source of internal discomfort

indicators.note: edited out of means cut from, so this letter is taken away from the pool
broadcast means scattered widely, so the remaining letters are spread anew

explanation.surface: A minute is cut from a cheerful daytime programme that causes indigestion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'edited from' removes M from CHIRPY DAYTIME and 'broadcast' rearranges the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Excess stomach acid causes heartburn and indigestion, a source of discomfort inside the body.
